featureRef: 14.12 Teacher requests a meeting with a guardian
name: Let a teacher raise a meeting with a guardian about something they have noticed, proposing the slot themselves
priorityReason: A concern a teacher has noticed reaches the family only if the teacher can raise it, rather than waiting to be asked.

goal.capability: to raise a meeting with a guardian when I have noticed something they need to know about
goal.outcome: the family is told the concern and offered a time, and a family that does not engage is visible to the school

secondaryActors.involvement: Is notified of the request and the proposed slot, confirms or declines it, and attends.
Sees requests and meetings for the sections they supervise, and sees where a request has gone unanswered.

additional.description: A request goes unanswered past the configured period and is surfaced to the coordinator (BR-8).
A teacher's approved leave removes a proposed slot.

preconditions.condition: The teacher teaches the student in a class or section assigned to them.
A published timetable exists, since the teacher's free slots are read from it.
The student's guardian holds a contact the request can be sent to.

postConditions: The request is on record against the student with the reason the teacher recorded.
The teacher selected the slot when raising it, which is the reverse of a guardian-requested meeting where the slot is offered in reply.
The slot proposed was one in which the teacher is genuinely free — not teaching, not covering, not on approved leave.
The guardian was told the reason and the proposed slot, and confirmed or declined it.
A guardian who declined could propose an alternative, and the teacher offered a further slot or closed the request.
On confirmation both sides were notified and a reminder was sent before the meeting.
A cancellation by either side released the slot and told the other.
After the meeting the teacher recorded that it took place and any note, held against the student and visible to the coordinator.

A request declined outright or left unanswered stayed visible to the teacher and the coordinator, since a family not engaging with a concern the school has raised is itself something the school needs to see.

screens.name: Request a meeting with a guardian

dataFields.name: Student
dataFields.validation: A student in a class or section the teacher teaches (BR-1).

dataFields.name: Reason
dataFields.validation: 20 to 1000 characters, written by the teacher. What the guardian reads before deciding (BR-3).
dataFields.example: Ayesha's work has fallen off sharply this month and she has been withdrawn in class. I would like to talk it through.

dataFields.name: Free slots
dataFields.validation: The slots in which the teacher is genuinely free, read from the timetable and excluding teaching, substitute cover and approved leave (BR-2).

dataFields.name: Proposed slot
dataFields.validation: Selected by the teacher when raising the request. The guardian confirms or declines it (BR-4).

dataFields.name: Proposed alternative
dataFields.validation: The time the guardian suggests instead, where they decline (BR-5).
dataFields.requiredWhen: The guardian declines and proposes an alternative

dataFields.name: Days unanswered
dataFields.validation: How long the request has gone without a response, shown to the teacher and the coordinator (BR-8).

dataFields.name: Cancellation reason
dataFields.validation: Maximum 250 characters, from whichever side cancels.
dataFields.example: Called away to a family emergency.

dataFields.name: Took place
dataFields.validation: Recorded by the teacher after the meeting (BR-7).

dataFields.name: Note
dataFields.validation: Maximum 1000 characters. Held against the student and visible to the coordinator (BR-7).
dataFields.example: Family aware of difficulties at home. Agreed to review in a fortnight.

entities.notes: One per request, with its reason, proposed slot, response and any note. Never deleted (BR-9).
Read to work out when the teacher is teaching (BR-2).
Read to exclude a slot the teacher is covering (BR-2).
Read to exclude a slot the teacher is on approved leave in (BR-2).
Read for the student and their guardian.
Held against the student and visible to the coordinator (BR-7).
The request, the response, any cancellation and the outcome.

permissions.rowScope: Students in classes and sections they teach.
permissions.notes: Raises the request, selects the slot, offers a further slot, closes the request, and records the outcome (BR-1).
Confirms or declines the proposed slot and may propose an alternative. Cannot raise a request through this route.
Sees requests and meetings, and sees where a request has gone unanswered (BR-8).
Reviews meeting activity and unanswered requests.

permissions.rowScope: No access. The meeting is between the guardian and the teacher.

businessRules.rule: A teacher raises a request about a student in a class or section they teach. A teacher who does not teach the student cannot raise one.

The system offers the slots in which the teacher is genuinely free, read from the published timetable and excluding any period in which they are teaching, are covering another class as a substitute, or are on approved leave.
The teacher records the reason. It is what the guardian reads before deciding, and a request arriving with no explanation invites a decline.

The teacher selects the slot when raising the request, and the guardian confirms or declines it. This is the reverse of a guardian-requested meeting, where the request arrives first and the slot is offered in reply.
A guardian who cannot attend may decline and propose an alternative time. The teacher then offers a further slot or closes the request.
Either side may cancel before the meeting. The slot is released and the other side is told.
After the meeting the teacher records that it took place and any note arising, held against the student and visible to the coordinator.

A request declined outright or left unanswered stays visible to the teacher and to the coordinator. A family not engaging with a concern the school has raised is itself something the school needs to see, and this has no equivalent in a guardian-requested meeting where an unanswered request is only the family's own to pursue.
A request is never deleted. A declined, closed or unanswered request stays on the record, which is what makes a pattern visible.

A proposed slot that later becomes unavailable — because the teacher's leave is approved, or their timetable changes — is released and both sides are told, rather than the request standing against a slot the teacher is no longer free in.
No coordinator approval is required for a teacher to raise a request. The coordinator sees what is happening; they do not gate it.
The guardian is told the reason at the same time as the proposed slot. A family asked to attend without being told why cannot judge whether they can.

transitions.condition: The guardian confirms the proposed slot (BR-4).
The guardian declines outright. It stays visible to the teacher and the coordinator (BR-8).
The guardian declines and proposes an alternative time (BR-5).
The teacher offers a further slot (BR-5).
The teacher closes the request rather than offering again.
Cancelled before the meeting. The slot is released and the other side is told (BR-6).
The slot passed and the guardian did not attend.

basicFlow.userAction: Opens the list of students in the classes and sections they teach and selects one.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Shows only students the teacher teaches.

basicFlow.navigation: My students → Request a meeting → Reason
basicFlow.userAction: Raises a meeting request with the guardian, recording the reason.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Requires the reason, which is what the guardian reads before deciding.
Offers the slots in which the teacher is genuinely free, excluding teaching, substitute cover and approved leave.

basicFlow.navigation: Request a meeting → Select a free slot → Send the request
basicFlow.userAction: Selects the slot when raising the request and sends it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Sends the reason and the proposed slot to the guardian together.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Portal → A meeting has been requested → Confirm
basicFlow.userAction: Reads the reason and the proposed slot and confirms it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Confirms the meeting and notifies both sides.
Notifies both sides on confirmation and sends a reminder before the meeting.

basicFlow.navigation: Portal → Cancel, or My meetings → Cancel
basicFlow.userAction: Cancels before the meeting where either side must.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Releases the slot and tells the other side.

basicFlow.navigation: Communication → Meetings I have raised → Record that it took place
basicFlow.userAction: Records that the meeting took place and any note arising.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Holds the note against the student, visible to the coordinator.

alternateFlows.condition: The guardian cannot attend at the proposed time
alternateFlows.navigation: A meeting has been requested → Decline and propose an alternative
alternateFlows.behaviour: They decline and suggest a time, and the teacher then offers a further slot or closes the request (BR-5).
alternateFlows.function: respondToMeetingRequest(requestId, 'Declined with an alternative proposed', alternative)

alternateFlows.navigation: A meeting has been requested → Decline
alternateFlows.behaviour: The request stays visible to the teacher and the coordinator, since a family not engaging with a concern is itself something the school needs to see (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: The guardian does not answer at all
alternateFlows.behaviour: The request is surfaced with how long it has gone unanswered. This has no equivalent in a guardian-requested meeting (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: The teacher is on approved leave that week
alternateFlows.behaviour: Those slots are not offered at all, since a slot proposed during leave is a meeting that will not happen (BR-2).

alternateFlows.condition: A confirmed slot later becomes unavailable
alternateFlows.behaviour: The slot is released and both sides are told, rather than the request standing against a slot the teacher is no longer free in (BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: The teacher offers a further slot after a decline
alternateFlows.navigation: Meetings I have raised → Offer another slot
alternateFlows.behaviour: A new slot is proposed and the guardian responds again (BR-5).

alternateFlows.condition: The guardian did not attend the confirmed slot
alternateFlows.navigation: Meetings I have raised → Record that it did not take place
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is recorded as not having happened and stays visible to the coordinator (BR-8).

exceptions.condition: The teacher selects a student they do not teach
exceptions.messageShown: You do not have permission to view this record.
Record the reason. The guardian reads it before deciding.

exceptions.condition: The teacher has no free slot at all in the period
exceptions.systemResponse: None is offered, and no request can be raised until one exists (BR-2).
exceptions.messageShown: You have no free slot this week. Try a later date range.

exceptions.condition: No timetable is published for the section
exceptions.systemResponse: Free slots cannot be worked out (BR-2).
exceptions.messageShown: No timetable is published. Free slots cannot be offered.

exceptions.condition: Two requests propose the same slot at once
exceptions.systemResponse: The second is refused, per concurrency-and-locking.
exceptions.messageShown: That slot has just been taken. Choose another.

exceptions.condition: The student's guardian holds no contact
exceptions.messageShown: This student has no guardian contact on file. The family cannot be reached.

exceptions.condition: The guardian declines with an alternative but gives no time
exceptions.systemResponse: The decline is recorded and the teacher is told no alternative was given.
exceptions.messageShown: Give a time you could attend, or decline without one.

exceptions.condition: The teacher records a note about a student they no longer teach
exceptions.messageShown: You do not have permission to view this record.
A meeting request is never deleted. A declined or unanswered one stays on the record.

departures.requirement: The guardian receives the reason at the same moment as the proposed slot. A family asked to attend without being told why cannot judge whether they can.

A declined or unanswered request stays visible to the teacher and the coordinator indefinitely, and is surfaced with how long it has gone unanswered. This is the asymmetry with a guardian-requested meeting and is deliberate.
A slot is proposed only where the teacher is not teaching, not covering and not on leave.
No coordinator approval is required for a teacher to raise a request. The coordinator sees what is happening; they do not gate it.
Requests and their notes are retained for the academic session and 3 years afterwards, since a note about a child is part of their record.

openQuestions.question: After how many days is an unanswered request surfaced to the coordinator?
What does the coordinator do with a family that repeatedly does not engage? Nothing acts on the visibility.
How many times may a teacher offer a further slot before the request must be closed?
Should the guardian see the note the teacher recorded, or is it internal?
openQuestions.assumption: Internal as modelled, visible to the coordinator only. This matters more here than in a guardian-requested meeting, since the concern is the school's.

openQuestions.question: May a coordinator raise a request on a teacher's behalf?

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
